title: rerank dim triage scratchpad
content:
One-line summary:
Ran into a reranker failure that surfaced as: dimension mismatch on the server path (expected 1536, got 768) plus intermittent p95 latency spikes (~600ms -> ~3.2s). Short-term workaround: pin embed model to embed-1536-v2 in the rerank pipeline. Long-term: add validation in SDK and CI, and fix model alias mapping that caused a wrong fallback.

Timeline and quick notes:
- 2026-03-05 09:12 UTC: First customer report (chatted with CS) — user saw rerank exceptions after weekly deploy.
- 2026-03-05 09:30: Confirmed locally using their minimal repro; error deterministic for their dataset but intermittent for our standard bench.
- 2026-03-05 11:00: Found change in model-mapping config (recent PR merged 2026-03-04) that touched alias-to-model lookups.
- 2026-03-06 15:20: Verified rollback to previous mapping removes dimension error but latency regression persists for some traffic.

Reproduction steps (minimal):
1) curl to embeddings endpoint (hosted) with their input set (short, mixed-English/emoji):

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model": "text-embed-auto", "input": ["Question A?", "Answer: OK 👍"] }'

Expected: embedding vectors length 1536. Observed: one-off responses with length 768. Example response snippet: 
{
  "data": [ { "embedding": [0.0034, -0.0021, ...], "index": 0 } ],
  "model": "text-embed-legacy-768",
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 12}
}

2) Python local check (used requests + numpy):

import requests
resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json={"model":"text-embed-auto","input":["a"]})
emb = resp.json()['data'][0]['embedding']
print(len(emb))  # -> sometimes 768, sometimes 1536

Observed server log snippet (prod rerank service):

2026-03-05T09:27:03Z ERROR rerank.pipeline - vectorize() failed: expected_dim=1536 actual_dim=768 trace_id=01FZQ3...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/rerank/pipeline.py", line 218, in _embed_batch
    assert vec.shape[1] == self.model_config.embedding_dim
AssertionError:  # triggered when fallback mapping used

Also saw these latency patterns on the same traces: p50 120ms p95 jump 3.2s for those failing batch calls. Non-failing batches stay ~110-220ms.

What I tried so far (commands & small changes):
- Reproduced locally against staging & prod (same intermittent dim mismatch).
- Forced model param to explicit name (embed-1536-v2) at client -> consistently returns 1536-dim and rerank proceeds.
- Reverted the model-mappings PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-mappings/pull/78) to previous commit -> reduced dim mismatch errors in canary cluster.
- Added logging around alias resolution in gateway: prints resolved_model when request arrives. Verified some requests resolving to text-embed-legacy-768 during peak churn.
- Increased embedding timeout in rerank worker (temp) to rule out partial/streamed responses causing truncated vectors — no change.
- Dumped raw response body from embedding service in failing cases -> full array present, length 768 (not truncated).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Alias resolution regression: 'text-embed-auto' can map to multiple implementations; a recent mapping allowed legacy 768 model to be chosen for certain inputs (fast path) when capacity low. This directly causes dim mismatch. Evidence: revert PR reduces errors; gateway logs show resolved_model as legacy in failing traces.

2) Model-selection fallback under high concurrency: the router may pick an available smaller model (768) to reduce latency/cost but the rerank pipeline expects 1536. There's no compatibility matrix enforced. Evidence: spikes correlate with capacity pressure windows.

3) Serialization/dtype bug: embeddings service returns nested float16 in some runs — but I ruled this out because lengths (not dtypes) differ and payloads parse fine.

4) Batch packing bug in rerank worker: if we concatenate batched embeddings from different providers we might not check per-item length. Less likely because server-side assertion triggers per-batch and reported actual_dim constant for whole batch (768).

Timing experiments (bench notes):
- Single small input -> embed-1536-v2 -> median 95ms (staging).
- Same call when router returns legacy-768 -> median 48ms (fast), but downstream rerank fails -> client perceives overall error.
- Under burst test (200 concurrent embedding requests): router started returning legacy-768 for ~18% of requests. That aligns with customer window.

Quick mitigation (prod):
- Patch: temporarily pin embed model in rerank config to embed-1536-v2 (deployed 2026-03-06 18:00 UTC) -> dimension errors dropped to <0.1% but costs rose ~2.7% because we stopped cheap fallbacks.
- Add a guard in rerank worker: if dim != expected then escalate via metric + return non-500 soft-fail response (so clients can degrade), and emit a detailed trace id to logs. Deployed as a hotfix to canary.

Longer-term fixes / TODOs:
- Add model compatibility matrix in gateway + router: explicit allowed embeddings dims per consumer (rerank, semantic-search, etc.).
- Enforce verification in SDK: when calling embeddings endpoint for a downstream that expects N dims, add optional header x-expected-embedding-dim. Gateway will validate and reject mismatches.
- Add e2e test that runs the full pipeline (embed -> rerank) and fails CI if any model alias maps to incompatible dims. Add to nightly smoke.
- Update runbooks: include how to triage mapping regressions and how to pin models per service.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Was the model-mappings PR intended to prioritize lower-cost models for small inputs? Need to find the design doc and confirm intended behavior. (Pinged Marco and Sana.)
- Are there legitimate workflows that accept 768 embeddings for rerank? If so, we need optional compatibility logic in rerank (project up to design).
- Does dedicated/dedicated-private behavior differ? Early check: private deployments have static mappings and didn't show the issue (suggesting mapping churn in hosted service is the cause).

Notes for follow-ups:
- Sanity check: grep logs for resolver decisions around 2026-03-05 09:00-10:00 UTC: gateway resolved_model entries exist for failing traces. Save those trace ids and link to Linear ticket.
- Add metric: embedding_dim_mismatch.count by service/route -> alarm at >5/min.
- Consider adding an indicator in model catalog UI that shows embedding_dim per model to reduce human error.

References & links: model-mapping PR, Linear ticket, Slack thread (above).

Immediate action items (owner assignments):
- Alyssa: finish alias resolution audit (today).
- Marco: follow up on PR intent & revert plan for staged mapping rollout (today).
- Sana: add canary alert for embedding dim mismatch + create dashboard panel (tomorrow).

Scratch area (raw commands I ran):
# reproduce exact single-request failing case
python - <<'PY'
import requests, os
url = 'https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer '+os.environ['STAGE_TOKEN'], 'Content-Type':'application/json'}
for i in range(20):
    r = requests.post(url, json={'model':'text-embed-auto','input':['test '+str(i)]}, headers=headers)
    j = r.json()
    m = j.get('model')
    d = len(j['data'][0]['embedding'])
    print(i, m, d)
PY

# quick curl we used in Canaries
curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STAGE_TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"text-embed-auto","input":["why is my reranker failing? emoji 👍"] }' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length, .model'

Last checked: 2026-03-11 10:02 UTC - opened Linear RIF-1452, assigned.

If anyone picks this up: start by checking gateway alias logs and the model-mappings history (git blame + PR description). I've left a few sample failing trace ids in the canary logs under /logs/rerank/canary/2026-03-05 (search for expected_dim=1536 actual_dim=768).

-- Alyssa
